issues.legal_issue: A person who represents a deceased party’s estate may qualify as a legal representative even if that person is not the head or administrator of the family.
material_facts: The defendant died while a recovery suit was pending.
Under the inheritance law applicable to the estate, the defendant’s widow held a share in it, while the remaining share devolved on the defendant’s children.
The widow was proposed as a substitute for the deceased defendant, although she was not the head of the family or administrator of the other heirs.
issues.conclusion: The widow qualified as a legal representative because her share in the estate meant that she represented the deceased defendant’s estate.
issues.legal_principle: The Civil Procedure Code’s definition of “legal representative” in Section 2(11) is inclusive and broad: it covers a person who represents the deceased’s estate, whether or not that person is an heir, and may include an heir who represents the estate. The Court relied on Daya Ram v. Shyam Sundari, [1965] 1 SCR 231, and N.K. Mohd. Sulaiman v. N.C. Mohd. Ismail, [1966] 1 SCR 937.

predicates.pending_civil_suit_when_party_died: A party died while a civil suit against that party was pending.
predicates.proposed_representative_had_a_share_in_t: The person proposed to represent the deceased party held a share in the deceased party’s estate.

issues.definition: When a party dies during a pending civil suit and the proposed representative held a share in that party’s estate, the proposed representative qualifies as a legal representative.

issues.legal_issue: A suit does not become defective merely because only some of the deceased defendant’s estate representatives were brought on record in time and the remaining heirs were added later.
material_facts: The defendant died while the recovery suit was pending.
After learning of the death, the plaintiff made a timely application to substitute the widow, who held a share in the estate and represented it.

The plaintiff made a bona fide inquiry and initially understood that the widow was the sole legal representative; after learning that the deceased had children, the plaintiff applied to add them as well.

The trial court allowed the application to set aside abatement and directed that the other heirs be added; the reviewing court set that order aside solely because the widow was not the head or administrator of the family.
issues.conclusion: Because the widow was brought on record in time and represented the estate, adding the other heirs later did not invalidate the proceedings; the suit could proceed on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XXII Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a deceased defendant’s legal representatives may be brought on record. The Court applied the principle in Daya Ram v. Shyam Sundari, [1965] 1 SCR 231, that heirs brought on record after bona fide inquiry may represent the entire estate in the absence of fraud or collusion, and relied also on N.K. Mohd. Sulaiman v. N.C. Mohd. Ismail, [1966] 1 SCR 937. It approved Mannem Venkataramaih v. M. Munnemma, AIR 1963 AP 406.

rule.if: defendant_died_during_pending_civil_suit and timely_added_person_represented_estate and bona_fide_inquiry_made and remaining_heirs_added_later

predicates.defendant_died_during_pending_civil_suit: A defendant died while a civil suit against that defendant was pending.
predicates.timely_added_person_represented_estate: A person who represented the deceased defendant’s estate was brought on record in time.
predicates.bona_fide_inquiry_made: The plaintiff made a bona fide inquiry to identify the deceased defendant’s legal representatives.
predicates.remaining_heirs_added_later: The plaintiff sought to add other heirs after the representative brought on record in time.

issues.definition: If a defendant dies during a pending civil suit, an estate representative is brought on record in time after a bona fide inquiry, and other heirs are added later, the suit may proceed on its merits.
